prompts.title: Comment code thoroughly (standards and version naming)
prompts.description: Rules for file headers, function docs, inline notes, TODOs and versioned file names.
prompts.template:
When you write code, always include clear, concise comments throughout the entire file(s) so that context is carried end-to-end. Use the following rules:

At the top of the file, add a brief header comment describing:
- Overall purpose of the script/module
- Key responsibilities and data flows
- Any important assumptions or external dependencies

For every function, method, or class:
Add a doc-style comment immediately above it explaining:
- What it does and why it exists
- Parameters and return values (including types if known)
- Common edge cases and constraints
- Possible exceptions or failure conditions and how they're handled

For non-obvious logic blocks (loops, conditionals, complex calculations, async flows, external API calls):
Add inline comments summarizing:
- The intent of the block (not restating the code)
- Any tricky behavior, side effects, or performance trade-offs
- Any assumptions about input shape, ordering, or state

Whenever you introduce new variables, data structures, or configuration, add a short comment where they are defined that explains:
- Their purpose and how they're used
- Expected value ranges, formats, or units

If you skip handling a known edge case or future enhancement, add a clear TODO comment describing:
- What's missing
- Why it's safe for now
- How you'd address it later

Make comments:
- Accurate and kept in sync with the code you generate
- High-signal and non-redundant (do not narrate every line; explain intent, design decisions, and caveats)

Output must always include these comments in the final code, not just in your explanation text.

In addition, include comments about revisions, error history, and version changes (for context).

As you create revisions of files, do not just reuse the same file name. Also include the version name as it comes, for better organization.

prompts.title: 📝 Anti-AI writing style guide
prompts.description: Phrases, words and punctuation to avoid so writing sounds like a person wrote it.
prompts.template:
{{task}}

📝 Anti-AI Detection Style Guide: word exclusions for common ChatGPT words

1. Words & Phrases to Avoid
These expressions are overused in AI-generated writing and make content sound generic. Replace or rephrase them.

Cliché transitions
- “At the end of the day”
- “With that being said”
- “It goes without saying”
- “In a nutshell”
- “Needless to say”
- “When it comes to”
- “On the other hand”
- “As a matter of fact”

Filler quantifiers
- “A significant number of”
- “It’s worth mentioning”
- “Last but not least”

Buzzwords & corporate jargon
- “Cutting-edge”
- “Leveraging”
- “Moving forward” / “Going forward”
- “Seamless integration”
- “Robust framework”
- “Holistic approach”
- “Paradigm shift”
- “Synergy”
- “Scale-up”
- “Optimize”
- “Game-changer”

Formal/academic filler
- “Notwithstanding”
- “In the realm of”
- “Takeaway”
- "Best Regards"
👉 Tip: Instead of defaulting to these phrases, use plain, direct language or more specific descriptions.

2. Punctuation Rules
- Replace em dashes (—) with commas, parentheses, or rewrites.
- Avoid semicolons in casual contexts; prefer periods or conjunctions.
- Remove ellipses (…) unless deliberately showing hesitation.
- Limit parenthetical asides; fold info into the main sentence.
- Use colons sparingly; don’t overuse for lists or emphasis.

3. Language Rules
- Replace hedging phrases (e.g., “however,” “it’s worth noting”) with direct statements.
- Avoid stock transitions (“furthermore,” “in conclusion”) unless needed.
- Vary terms; don’t repeat the same phrase.
- Use contractions in informal writing (e.g., “don’t” vs. “do not”).
- Swap formal words (“utilize,” “ascertain”) for simpler ones (“use,” “find out”).

4. Style Rules
- Prefer concise, varied sentence lengths over rigid structures.
- Allow imperfections: fragments, casual tone, natural flow.
- Adjust tone to fit the audience (formal or conversational).
- Keep the core message intact, but avoid sounding polished to the point of sterility.

5. Example Fix
Before (AI-like):
“The results—though preliminary—suggest success; however, it’s worth noting limitations.”
After (Human-like):
“The preliminary results suggest success, but the limitations still need attention.”

✅ Quick Checklist for Editing
- Did I cut out clichés and filler phrases?
- Did I simplify overly formal words?
- Did I vary sentence lengths and rhythms?
- Does the text sound like something a person would naturally say?

---
In the results please refrain from using these phrases attached, and the words below between the colon ":" and the 3 greater than signs ">>>" below:

:
Explore, Revolutionize, Landscape, Delve, Dive, Uncover, Discover, unleash, ultimate, innovative and unique approach, unlock, elevate, introducing, delightful, ignite, empower, limitless, harnessing, memorable, extraordinary, decode, blend, indulge, effortless, await, enjoy, irresistible, hassle-free, tailored, unforgettable, meaningful, impactful, Step into, Capture

>>>

Please also limit the use of exclamation marks so that it looks more conversational than an ad.

fields.label: What should be written?
fields.description: Leave blank to use this as a standing style guide for the rest of the chat.
